title: Netanyahu Says Officials Feared 'Annoying Hamas' by Waking Him Before Oct. 7, Later Denies Alleging 'Betrayal'
detail: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Tuesday, September 1, 2026 that senior IDF and defense officials 'deliberately chose not to wake him' in the hours before the October 7, 2023 attack because 'they knew that, as prime minister of Israel, I would have immediately given the order to put the entire military on alert' — adding 'I would have woken up all the communities, woken up all the security coordinators and told the air force to be ready to strike' anyone approaching the Gaza fence. Later that evening, after the remarks drew accusations that he was alleging betrayal by security chiefs, Netanyahu released a video clarifying: 'They have asked me several times, do I think there was a betrayal, and I said no, I don't think there was a betrayal, I think there was a failure, a great failure,' saying officials held off waking him 'because of a fear of a miscalculation, so as not to annoy Hamas.' Netanyahu's office has previously acknowledged his intelligence officer received an IDF memo about suspicious Hamas activity roughly three hours before the attack but did not pass it to the prime minister. Then-Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar stated in an April 2025 affidavit that at 3:03 a.m. on October 7 all security agencies were alerted to 'unusual preparations and the possibility of offensive intentions by Hamas,' and that at 5:15 a.m. he 'instructed that the Prime Minister's military secretary be updated.' Israeli media described the statements as a deliberate effort by the Netanyahu family to reframe the October 7 failure narrative ahead of the October 27, 2026 election, with a Likud source reportedly telling Channel 12 there is 'a decision by the family to spread conspiracy theories in the time leading up to the election to distance Netanyahu from the massacre at any cost.'

title: Sara Netanyahu Suggests Opposition Leader Golan Had Advance Knowledge of Oct. 7; Golan Warns of $825,000 Defamation Suit
detail: During a Channel 14 interview on Monday, August 31, 2026, Prime Minister Netanyahu's wife Sara Netanyahu insinuated without evidence that Democrats party leader Yair Golan — a retired IDF major general, former deputy chief of staff, and Netanyahu's chief election rival for the October 27, 2026 vote — had advance knowledge of the October 7, 2023 attack, citing his early arrival at the Nova festival massacre site: 'When you're a military man of such high rank, claiming that you fought on October 7, already early in the morning you were there, already dressed and ready at a very, very early hour.' Golan drove to the Nova site around 8 a.m. on October 7 — roughly 90 minutes after the attack began — and rescued multiple people. On September 1, 2026, Golan sent Sara Netanyahu a formal legal warning threatening a NIS 2.5 million ($825,000) defamation suit unless she retracted the claim, apologized, and made a substantial donation to Nova festival survivors, writing on X that 'Sara Netanyahu spread a false conspiracy in an attempt to rewrite October 7, turning those who went out to save lives into traitors.' Sara Netanyahu refused to apologize and issued her own legal warning demanding NIS 100,000 in compensation and a retraction, threatening to countersue Golan for NIS 1 million, with a spokesperson saying she 'never spread conspiracy theories, but spoke only about solid facts that are undisputed in Israel.'

media.caption: Yair Golan, Democrats party leader and Netanyahu election rival, warned Sara Netanyahu of a defamation suit over her Oct. 7 conspiracy claim, September 1, 2026
